executiveSummary: GM1948 passes the complete deterministic execution contract across all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, generalized boundary, 84,711 residents, 93 neighbourhoods, four BAG places, 57 BRT settlement labels, Brabant-Noord assignment, seven NWB logical links, zero active ProRail stations and 81 GTFS stop areas reconcile. Release remains correction-required. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset holds 0.901067 metres of local flood depth from T+24 through T+72, reaches 26,629 affected people-equivalent and 1,771,249.295 event-attributable person-hours, but selects no EDO-36 breach, Maas level, connected footprint, Aa/Dommel backwater, Zuid-Willemsvaart/sluis state, regional defence, arrival or recession. Official local evidence instead distinguishes runoff from high paved ground to low edges, low-lying business parks, the Aa through Veghel, the Dommel through Sint-Oedenrode, canal controls and two water-board systems. Eight unrelated T+24 presets reuse one complete 93-neighbourhood order. A focused source inside a current TOP10NL mixed-forest polygon in BU19480106 Buitengebied Hurkske en Hoek produces nonzero direct flame but ranks its source neighbourhood only 61st. Public water, transport, grid, antenna, school and care records materially improve context but do not establish live topology, capacity, passability, backup or recovery. Unknown and NoData must never become zero, safe, open or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: Official GM1948 2025 municipality, neighbourhood and BAG context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS areas/statistics 2025; BAG and PDOK snapshots used by deployment
supports: The annual machine-readable CC BY 4.0 CBS release identifies GM1948 as Meierijstad and reports 84,711 residents, density 460 per square kilometre, 22.8% aged 65 or older and 12,044 one-person households.

The reference point [5.4973311484891685, 51.590375653298985] and centres of Erp, Schijndel, Sint-Oedenrode and Veghel lie inside the 2025 generalized municipality. BAG woonplaatsen are Public Domain Mark 1.0; CBS/PDOK generalized areas are CC BY 4.0.

Ninety-three published neighbourhood rows sum to 84,705 residents, six below the municipal control (-0.007%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 84,711. Published rounding, suppression, unavailable and not-applicable values retain their source semantics.

CBS counts do not identify incident-time workers, visitors, pupils, care recipients, medically dependent residents, responders, institutional occupants, household stocks or people requiring evacuation assistance.

evidenceSources.title: NWB, rail and scheduled public-transport inputs for Meierijstad
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS deployment snapshots inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates seven logical boundary links to six municipalities: three A50 segments to Maashorst, Bernheze and Son en Breugel, N279 segments to Laarbeek and Bernheze, N617 to Sint-Michielsgestel and N618 to Boxtel.

The three A50 links and two N279 links are series directions of physical corridors, not additive municipal capacity. Their 260/150 nominal values are synthetic transfer ceilings, not traffic counts, emergency throughput or utility topology.

Zero ProRail stations is coherent with the former Duits Lijntje having lost passenger service in 1950 and freight service in 2004. Eighty-one GTFS stop areas, including Veghel Busstation and village stops, are timetable context only and do not prove event-time service, vehicle capacity or accessibility.
NWB does not resolve internal bridge/canal crossing state, destination acceptance or emergency routing; a schedule or absent bounded NDW situation is never proof that a route is open.

evidenceSources.title: Programma Water en Riolering Meierijstad
evidenceSources.edition: In force from 4 February 2022; current version inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official programme records a 2021 impact analysis for water nuisance, heat, drought and flooding and directs users to the As50+ climate atlas. A public rule text does not establish a blanket machine-data licence for every embedded study or layer; each downloadable layer needs separate reuse review.

Meierijstad's buildings largely follow higher longitudinal dunes. Runoff from high, often paved areas accumulates at lower edges; expansion-district storage is often at their edges and low-lying business parks contribute materially to water nuisance and heat stress.

Named issues include little sewer storage, excessive paving, sewer overflows and Kienehoef/Dommelrode. The programme says detailed heavy-rain water-on-street evidence was not yet available when written; later data must be acquired and versioned rather than inferred from the policy text.

A loam-bearing substrate under the settlement ridges can make damaged layers drain groundwater and affect settlement, foundations, pipes, sewers and pavement. The programme separately records De Leijgraaf north of Erp/Veghel and a Bloemenwijk case where sewer replacement changed drainage and caused groundwater nuisance.
The regulation is static planning evidence, not a current rain observation, sewer model, incident map, capacity test, maintenance state or T+72 drainage forecast.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap De Dommel / Waterschap Aa en Maas
evidenceSources.title: Klimaatrobuust Beekdal Sint-Oedenrode and Aa-dal project context
evidenceSources.edition: Current official project pages inspected 3 September 2026; Aa-dal uitvoeringsagenda 2022
supports: The Dommel runs east-west through built-up Sint-Oedenrode. Official T100 calculations found part of the centre could inundate; the project distinguishes Rijsingen, De Neul, Omgeving Hambrug and 't Laar and describes a 25-metre winter bed, high-water channel, extended bridges, raised/new defences and a reconnected dead arm.

Completed measures and a design return period do not prove a present all-clear, event footprint, defence condition or passability. De Dommel distinguishes street water, groundwater response, overflowing brooks/ditches and regional defence responsibility.

Aa en Maas identifies the Aa through Veghel between Erp and A50, water-nuisance locations along it, water-storage need, and 't Ham storage. Its project agenda seeks brook restoration and higher spring groundwater while noting urban limits.

The two authorities and municipality therefore require separate catchment, channel, defence, asset, rainfall and groundwater evidence. Their pages declare planning/project state, not live gate/pump operation or calibrated local impacts; no blanket data licence was established for page content.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024–2027, first-72-hour resilience and public danger guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2024–2027; current municipal and VRBN pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The regional worst case is an EDO-36 Maas event, while the profile separately emphasizes Aa, Dommel and Dieze regional defences and says local scenario probability and impact can differ from regional assessment. It calls for more insight into effects on gas/electricity and better partner information.

The nature-fire measure is a 200-hectare forest/heath fire under extreme dryness, strong wind and difficult access; the region states the risk is in forest/heath parcels and may involve campsites, recreation/military functions and homes in wooded settings. This is an official scenario class, not a current ignition or footprint.

VRBN's 2025 resilience discussion explicitly focuses on groups less able to manage the first 72 hours and on a social emergency kit/network map. Public current material on long power outage says several fire stations still require technical/financial work for generator connection; regional readiness is not uniform site-level backup.

Meierijstad instructs people to follow siren, NL-Alert, sound-truck and Brabant Alert messages, go indoors and close windows/doors/ventilation, and wait for an official all-clear. Guidance is not evidence a warning was issued, received or acted upon, nor that household stocks exist.

The policy/pages do not publish a municipality-specific machine incident/action feed or blanket reuse licence. Plan roles must become time-stamped assignments and confirmations before affecting simulation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards
evidenceSources.title: Zuid-Willemsvaart, Waterinfo observations and public water-control/wastewater context
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo retrieved 2 September 2026; HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Rijkswaterstaat identifies the Zuid-Willemsvaart as a controlled navigation route from Maastricht to 's-Hertogenbosch, with current water levels, shipping notices and bridge/lock operating information and the Maxwell Taylorbrug in Veghel. Static corridor facts do not prove live passability or hydraulic connection to a selected flood event.

The CC0 Waterinfo snapshot contains six fresh GM1948 water-level observations at 2026-09-02T17:30Z: above/below locks at Erp sluis 5, Schijndel sluis/spuikanaal and Veghel sluis 4. Values range from 470 to 1273 cm NAP. They are point water levels, not local inundation depth, breach, threshold, discharge, forecast or control state.

The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 214 GM1948 points: nine sewer pumps, twelve surface-water pumps, one wastewater treatment and 192 weirs. It includes both Aa en Maas and De Dommel managers; 199 capacities are null.

Register presence, manager, status or capacity does not establish unit consistency, connectivity, setpoint, telemetry, backup, spare capacity, operator decision or restoration. Contributor completeness varies; absent objects and null fields remain Unknown/NoData.

evidenceSources.title: Electricity planning, acute care, telecom and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: The one NBNL postcode sample assigns Enexis service area ERD Eerde and reports 151.8 MW existing versus 156.4 MW required withdrawal, an 83 MW queue across 183 requests, 142.7/134.3 MW injection and 97.5 MW queued across 109 requests, plus nineteen projects earliest 2026. The map is open data but no exact licence identifier was found; capacity/projects update at least quarterly and queues monthly.

That single large-user planning sample is not a municipality-wide service area, substation, current load, household supply, outage, reserve or restoration forecast. Its point is the DUO postcode used for lookup, not an electricity asset.

RIVM's national questionnaire v1.1 is CC0 and has no emergency department inside GM1948. Straight-line reference-point distance is about 11.91 km to 24/7 Bernhoven in Uden, 14.00 km to Catharina Eindhoven and 18.46 km to Jeroen Bosch; distances and annual roles/visits are not ambulance routes, acceptance, staffing, occupancy or backup.

The deployment contains 144 RDI sites, including 71 mobile and 37 fixed-link sites, and 54 DUO education records. RDI states no fixed refresh or reuse licence; DUO is daily CC BY with version unspecified. Antennas and schools do not prove coverage, backhaul, power, shelter/distribution role, occupancy, staff, supplies or live status.

No current bounded NDW, KNMI warning/observation/seismic, air-quality or government-service record is assigned to GM1948. Empty assignment is time/coverage NoData, not open roads, safe air, no warning, no event or normal service.

evidenceSources.title: BRT TOP10NL terrain and BAG-geocoded local nature context
evidenceSources.edition: BRT TOP10NL OGC snapshot inspected 3 September 2026; selected feature registered 1 September 2024 from 2020 imagery
supports: BRT TOP10NL is CC BY 4.0. Feature e4fe0420-15b3-547e-b82f-de6fdeadd53d is classified bos: gemengd bos with 0.1-metre source accuracy and contains audit point [5.65225530494228, 51.57717290992305] inside BU19480106 Buitengebied Hurkske en Hoek.

The forest point is a controlled audit fixture in the Het Hurkske vicinity, not an observation, ignition, official incident scenario, hazard boundary or claim that the whole neighbourhood is combustible.

Terrain eligibility must be combined with a dated ignition/perimeter, fuel and moisture state, wind, access, exposure and response evidence; land-cover alone never predicts fire spread or T+72 recovery.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and 2025 editions agree.
notes: Feature id, municipality bundle and manifest all identify GM1948 / Meierijstad in Noord-Brabant and Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Noord.
BoundaryEdition and statisticsEdition are 2025; policy, observations, registers and the synthetic exercise clock retain separate valid times.
No code, name, province, safety-region, centre-containment or edition contradiction was found.

geography.summary: The generalized municipality and settlement centres are coherent, but Meierijstad spans distinct catchments, low/high terrain and controlled canals that require native geometry.
notes: The reference point and four BAG place centres are contained; the municipality has four districts and 93 neighbourhoods.
Official evidence distinguishes the Aa/Veghel, Dommel/Sint-Oedenrode, Leijgraaf, high settlement ridges, low edges/business parks, groundwater/loam and Zuid-Willemsvaart controls.
A municipality centroid or generalized boundary cannot select a breach, channel connection, defence state, surface-flow path, drainage catchment, lock/bridge state, forest source or road passability.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and rounded neighbourhood population reconciles within publication semantics.
notes: Generated/official population is 84,711, density 460 per square kilometre, age65Pct 22.8 and one-person households 12,044.
Ninety-three neighbourhood populations sum to 84,705 (-6, -0.007%); households sum to 37,075 and age65+ to 19,350. Deterministic local allocation closes exactly to the municipal control.
Largest neighbourhoods are Veghel Centrum 3,240, Kienehoef Zuid 2,465, Laarbunders 2,325, Boschweg Noordoost 2,300 and 't Ven West 2,215.
Resident aggregates omit pupils, industrial/logistics workers, visitors, acute-care load, home-care dependence, household emergency stocks and event-time mobility.

regionalDetail.summary: All 93 neighbourhoods load, but statistical gaps and public asset coverage remain explicitly non-operational.
notes: Most CBS fields cover 93/93; home value covers 89, cars per household 84, disability recipients 90, and housing/tenure/benefit fields mostly 90. District heating and public charging cover 0/93 and remain null, not zero.
The PWR notes distinct legacy systems and incomplete detailed rain evidence at publication; later municipal model/register data require their own edition and coverage.
Water points, Waterinfo, NBNL, antenna, school and care records remain typed context with affectsSimulation=false; none validates live topology, capacity, state or recovery.

settlements.summary: Four BAG places and 57 BRT labels are contained and preserve Meierijstad's dispersed multi-village structure.
notes: BAG places are Erp, Schijndel, Sint-Oedenrode and Veghel. BRT yields 31 buurtschappen, five deelkernen, eight gehuchten and thirteen woonkernen.
Labels include Boerdonk, Boskant, Eerde, Keldonk, Mariaheide, Nijnsel, Olland, Wijbosch, Zijtaart and many dispersed hamlets; none is silently collapsed into one urban centre.
Administrative/topographic membership does not establish incident-time population, isolation, reception capacity, service state or supply role.

transport.summary: Seven road-derived boundary links and scheduled bus access are reproducible, but crossings, internal access and destination state are unresolved.
notes: Seven NWB route records reach six neighbouring municipalities via A50, N279, N617 and N618; same-corridor series records are non-additive and all capacities are synthetic logical ceilings.
Zero active ProRail stations is coherent with the disused Duits Lijntje. Eighty-one GTFS stop areas do not establish incident operation, frequency, accessibility or evacuation throughput.
The graph omits internal Aa/Dommel and Zuid-Willemsvaart crossings, Maxwell Taylorbrug/locks, village roads, route-to-hospital acceptance and live incident restrictions.
Empty bounded NDW assignment is NoData, never an all-open assertion.

emergencyContext.summary: Official authorities and first-72-hour guidance exist, but no local trigger/action/resource/acceptance ledger enters the simulation.
notes: VRBN distinguishes EDO-36, regional-water, nature-fire and prolonged utility-outage pathways and explicitly prioritizes groups less self-reliant for the first 72 hours.

No warning, NL-Alert, water-board/RWS decision, canal/bridge closure, evacuation/shelter-in-place, welfare check, hospital transfer, temporary water, resupply, repair or mutual-aid item has an owner, trigger, resource, requested/confirmed/completed state, result or expiry.

No local acute department means Meierijstad depends on cross-boundary routes and acceptance, but straight-line distance and annual questionnaire fields cannot establish ambulance travel or incident capacity.
Preparedness instructions and registered schools/antennas are not evidence of household supplies, reception sites, communication continuity or completed actions.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets produce complete finite deterministic output at six checkpoints and eight services; evidence and realism failures are separate.
notes: The mandatory and focused gates executed severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Maximum checkpoint severity / maximum affected people-equivalent / T+72 event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.397495 / 12,754 / 603,237.842; pluvial 0.369546 / 8,967 / 549,663.196; river 0.283304 / 26,629 / 1,771,249.295; coastal 0.024820 / 0 / 132,483.823; heat 0.598267 / 4,297 / 411,243.499.
These are deterministic exercise outputs, not observed people/customers, forecasts, warnings, probabilities, casualties, damage assessments or operator restoration commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact zero-event behavior, reconciliation, causal ledgers and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: The initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1948 pnpm audit:model passed one file and two tests in 29.94 seconds, with 29.71 seconds test execution.
Every intensity-zero run has exactly zero event severity, affected people-equivalent and event-attributable deprivation; repeat output and web/core preset parity pass.
All 84,711 residents and 93 rows reconcile; demand/delivery closes, local hazard is selected-layer invariant, route ceilings hold and cumulative attributable person-hours are monotonic.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local calibration, live operations or evidential support.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A shared seeded neighbourhood order and centroid river screen contradict Meierijstad's source-specific water, terrain and fire geography.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire reuse the exact complete 93-neighbourhood order; the shared top five are Duin 1, Nijnsel, Buitengebied Oetelaar, Buitengebied Kraanmeer en Veluwe and Bunderse Hoek Zuid.
Official PWR/water-board evidence instead separates runoff to low edges/business parks, Aa, Dommel, Leijgraaf, groundwater/loam, canal controls and local interventions; none controls the rank.

The canonical wildfire has zero direct flame at T+24 and only remote smoke/drought. In a focused audit run at TOP10NL mixed-forest point [5.65225530494228, 51.57717290992305], direct flame is 0.229176, smoke 0.491360 and municipal severity 0.326674, but source neighbourhood BU19480106 ranks 61/93 while Duin 1 ranks first.
The focused ignition is a synthetic diagnostic fixture, not a current incident. It proves the allocator does not use source containment; it does not supply an official fire perimeter or forecast.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability is inspectable but unsupported by Meierijstad's actual utilities, water systems, routes and external care.
notes: River T+72 availability is power 0.663766, water 0.632568, drainage 0.468021, gas 0.779440, telecom 0.603120, mobility 0.762091, facilities 0.562739 and supply 0.602658; no operator or selected flood scenario validates those percentages.
Road-derived routes are limited to mobility and logistics supply but still omit internal crossing/destination state. HWH, Waterinfo, NBNL and RDI records remain non-causal context.
Acute care is cross-boundary and requires route, ambulance, acceptance/diversion, staffing, power/water/telecom/oxygen, medicines and backup/fuel state; all are absent.
Safe-to-publish operator topology, switching, stores, crews and restoration may be unavailable or security-sensitive; the fallback must remain transparently aggregate and synthetic.

causalTrace.summary: The river and local hazard outputs expose precision without the scenario dimensions needed to defend it.
notes: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset labels 0.901067 m as derived-screening and leaves unsupportedDimensions empty despite no EDO-36 breach/location, boundary hydrograph, Maas level/discharge, defence state, connected footprint, Aa/Dommel/canal linkage, arrival or recession.
Current six-point Waterinfo levels cannot calibrate a calendar-unbound 168-hour scenario and are not flood depths. Static projects, register points and policies cannot be fused into live consequence.
Pluvial, heat, winter, smoke and cyber ranks need hazard-specific forcing/targets and native spatial evidence; exact common-seed neighbourhood scores must not appear as supported local results.

Each observation, forecast, official scenario, register/context layer and synthetic assumption needs publisher, edition/version, retrieval, issue/valid time, spatial coverage/resolution, licence, evidence class and NoData.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood and compound plateaus plus rapid clearances have no local water, operator, route, care or action evidence.
notes: River T+72 retains severity 0.283304, flood depth 0.901067, pressure 0.363118, 26,629 affected people-equivalent and 1,771,249.295 attributable person-hours; facilities alone decline further between T+24 and T+72 while other service values remain fixed.
Compound T+24 to T+72 holds flood depth 0.323328 and all eight availabilities effectively fixed; T+72 severity/pressure/affected/person-hours is 0.339112 / 0.519548 / 45,298 / 2,842,241.518.

Storm, pluvial, winter, canonical wildfire and direct coastal severity clear by T+72, but no inspection, pumping/dewatering, bridge/road reopening, utility repair, hospital acceptance or official all-clear supports those trajectories.
Seventy-two hours is a preparedness and decision horizon, not an automatic recovery deadline. Actions must be event-driven and remain Unknown until assigned and confirmed.

findings.summary: The river preset presents an unsupported precise local flood depth and impact.
findings.evidence: The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel run holds 0.901067 m from T+24 through T+72 and reaches 26,629 affected people-equivalent. E03–E06 distinguish EDO-36, Aa, Dommel, Leijgraaf and Zuid-Willemsvaart pathways, but the run selects no breach, water level/discharge, defence, connected footprint, backwater/control state, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Suppress exact GM1948 direct depth/affected output or mark it unsupported/Unknown until a versioned named EDO-36 or local-water scenario is selected. Keep Maas primary-defence, Aa/Dommel regional-water, canal-control and pluvial/groundwater mechanisms separate.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one complete neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire have the identical 93-row T+24 rank led by Duin 1 and Nijnsel. Official evidence identifies mutually different terrain, catchment, drainage, forest, settlement and infrastructure mechanisms.
findings.action: Remove the shared seeded local hazard multiplier. Ingest per-hazard source surfaces/targets or show a uniform/Unknown local result; assert rank diversity and intersection with supported footprints.

findings.summary: A local forest ignition does not prioritize its containing neighbourhood.
findings.evidence: At a point inside current TOP10NL mixed forest and BU19480106 Buitengebied Hurkske en Hoek, a controlled T+24 wildfire returns direct flame 0.229176 and smoke 0.491360 yet ranks the source neighbourhood 61/93; Duin 1 is first. The source is a synthetic diagnostic, not an incident.
findings.action: Use a licensed fuel/combustible-area mask, dated ignition/perimeter, moisture, wind and access. Assert source containment and finite distance/wind spread; absent ignition/perimeter remains Unknown rather than no-risk or remote smoke.

findings.summary: Pluvial and groundwater precision lacks the municipality's actual surface/sewer model.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.312813 m and 8,967 affected people-equivalent using the shared order. The current PWR names high-to-low runoff, business-park edges, sewer storage/overflows, loam/groundwater and specific areas, but no rain hyetograph, AHN/BGT surface, inlet/sewer model or antecedent groundwater drives output.
findings.action: Integrate versioned As50+/municipal BRP or 3Di results with rainfall design, sewer-included flag, terrain, saturation/groundwater, resolution, coverage and licence. Otherwise suppress exact local depth and affected counts.

findings.summary: Exact utility and T+72 restoration values have no operator evidence.
findings.evidence: Eight exact river T+72 availability values are emitted although public HWH, Waterinfo, Enexis/NBNL and RDI records provide no physical utility topology, incident outage, backup, switching, controls, crews, stores or restoration commitment.
findings.action: Keep public records affectsSimulation=false. Label service/recovery values aggregate synthetic assumptions and accept only authorized, time-scoped operator aggregates/manual incident overrides; absent state remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Water and electricity public records are useful context but incomplete and non-operational.
findings.evidence: HWH contains 214 points and 199 null capacities; Waterinfo supplies six dated lock levels; NBNL supplies one postcode sample with substantial queues. None is live network capacity or a selected event state, and coverage varies.
findings.action: Retain source collection, feature meaning, licence, retrieval/valid time, coverage and nulls. Seek authority-approved catchment/service-area aggregates; never sum unknown/unitless capacities or turn absent observations into safety.

findings.summary: Road-derived regional links omit internal crossings, public transport operation and destination acceptance.
findings.evidence: Seven A50/N279/N617/N618 logical records are traceable but non-additive by physical corridor. The graph has no internal Aa/Dommel/Zuid-Willemsvaart crossing or bridge/lock state, and GTFS plus zero active railway stations does not establish emergency accessibility.
findings.action: Retain NWB only for mobility/logistics supply with physical-corridor identity. Add incident-valid bridge/lock/road/transit and critical-destination state where public/authorized; otherwise show passability and capacity Unknown.

findings.summary: External acute care is not represented as a route-dependent first-72-hour service.
findings.evidence: RIVM has no local SEH; Bernhoven is approximately 11.91 km straight-line from the municipal reference point, with other regional alternatives farther away. The model has no ambulance travel, destination acceptance/diversion, staffing, critical utilities, oxygen, medicines or backup state.
findings.action: Add authorized aggregate facility role, live acceptance/diversion, route/access and critical utility/supply state with valid time. Missing fields remain Unknown; a point, annual questionnaire or distance never guarantees care.

findings.summary: Unsupported river and local spatial dimensions are hidden behind precise maps.
findings.evidence: River uses spatialEvidence=derived-screening and unsupportedDimensions=[] despite missing event/footprint dimensions. Synthetic local ranks and service percentages remain available across map layers without an adjacent municipality-specific Unknown warning.
findings.action: Populate unsupported dimensions and surface the limitation beside maps, briefs and exports. Preserve evidence class, publisher, version, retrieval/valid time, resolution/coverage, licence and NoData throughout.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger represents Meierijstad's documented roles and distributed villages.
findings.evidence: VRBN and Meierijstad publish response roles, warning channels and 72-hour resilience aims, but no modeled item records trigger, authority, assignment, resource, state, result or expiry for water, fire, access, care, shelter/welfare, resupply or utility repair.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records for warning/all-clear, water/defence/canal decisions, fire source/perimeter and access, village welfare/evacuation or shelter-in-place, care transfer, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.

corrections.summary: Replace the unsupported GM1948 river screen with named EDO-36 and local-water evidence semantics.
corrections.validation: Without a selected versioned connected scenario, GM1948 exact direct river depth and affected count render unsupported/Unknown. EDO-36, Aa, Dommel, canal-control and pluvial pathways remain distinct and fixtures preserve footprint, arrival, duration, recession and NoData.

corrections.summary: Remove the shared local rank and add hazard-specific Meierijstad geometry.
corrections.validation: Unrelated hazards no longer share one complete order; supported water fixtures intersect their named catchments/low areas and a Hurkske forest-source fixture prioritizes BU19480106 with bounded wind/distance spread.

corrections.summary: Keep HWH, Waterinfo, grid, antenna, school and care records context-only with strict time and NoData semantics.
corrections.validation: Cards/exports show publisher, edition/version, retrieval and valid time, evidence class, coverage/resolution, licence and affectsSimulation=false; null/empty fields never display as zero, safe, open, available or restored.

corrections.summary: Represent internal crossings and external acute-care dependencies without inventing topology.
corrections.validation: A50/N279/N617/N618 remain non-additive road proxies; canal/brook crossings, public transport and hospital route/acceptance/backup state have time-scoped evidence or explicit Unknown and affect outcomes only after confirmed state.

corrections.summary: Implement a role-aware Unknown-first first-72-hour action and resource ledger for GM1948.
corrections.validation: At each checkpoint warnings, water/fire/access decisions, village welfare, care transfer, shelter/reception, resupply and repairs show authority, trigger, assignment, resource, status, result, valid time and expiry; missing facts remain Unknown.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Enexis, Brabant Water, gas, telecom, sewer/drainage or facility topology, live control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Meierijstad flood consequences depend on a named Maas/EDO-36 event or local Aa/Dommel/canal/rain/groundwater mechanism, connected defences and controls; static policy and project pages are not incident forecasts.
HWH completeness varies, 199 of 214 local capacities are null, and registered values/statuses do not establish comparable throughput or operation.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM aggregates omit incident-time workers, pupils, visitors, patients, home-care dependency, shelters, response resources and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and person-hours is weighted local pre-network service deprivation, not casualties, evacuees, patients or observed customer interruptions.
Weather, warning, road, water, air, grid and facility state changes after retrieval; stale or out-of-coverage data must degrade to Unknown rather than persist or clear automatically.
provinceReviewFlags: Define Brabant-wide semantics separating Maas/EDO-36 primary-defence flooding from Aa/Dommel/Dieze regional water, canals, pluvial runoff and groundwater; require named connected event footprints.
Coordinate Aa en Maas, De Dommel, Rijkswaterstaat and municipal evidence contracts at their shared boundaries, including channel/control/defence ownership, version, valid time, licence and NoData.
Ingest/review As50+ stress-test data and assert high-to-low runoff, business-park edge and sewer/groundwater mechanisms without converting design events into current conditions.
Test the shared neighbourhood rank defect across Noord-Brabant urban, rural, water, heat, cyber and nature-fire contexts; include an official combustible-area source-containment fixture.

Audit A50/N279 and Zuid-Willemsvaart/internal crossing dependencies plus external Bernhoven/Jeroen Bosch/Catharina acute-care access without turning roads, schedules or annual facility records into guaranteed availability.

Require Unknown-first first-72-hour actions and resources for distributed villages, less-self-reliant groups, water/fire decisions, warnings, hospital transfer, temporary water, reception and resupply.
